decisive_moments.reason: Pro clarified that evaluation-first means a lightweight, revisable baseline after an initial prototype, directly answering the strongest objection that early benchmarks may measure toy problems.

Con correctly identified the sequencing risk: early evaluation metrics may be obsolete before the task and failure distribution are understood, and argued coherently for co-evolution rather than rigid priority.
Pro narrowed the claim to measuring before consequential capability scaling and connected that sequencing to reliability, cost discipline, user protection, and production redesign costs.

flags.quote: late discovery of failures makes redesign expensive and can harm users
Early capability work can cheaply establish prototypes
